samples.reason: Implemented credential/session theft, archive submission, keylogging, remote tasking, unauthorized persistence and security-control disabling establish hostile intent.
samples.missing_context: Delivery, operator identity, victim environment and runtime success are unknown.
samples.marker_line: Salat RAT: credential theft; add recovery and UAC disable coverage
evidence: PE is 12,572,672 bytes, i386 GUI, unsigned; Go build/module identity salat. Independent Go pclntab recovery at file offset 0x8a2880 recovered 10,636 functions, including main.main at VA 0x8d5410.

main.getChromeLogins at 0x8f2e80 opens a SQL database, calls QueryContext, iterates Rows.Next/Scan and calls DecryptChrome. main.getChrome at 0x8f1350 dispatches logins, cookies, tokens and autofill collectors. Steal also collects wallet stores and Discord/Steam/Telegram session material.

main.Steal finalizes a ZIP, Base64-encodes it, constructs and marshals JSON, transforms it with main.dec and calls main.rq. tryRQ at 0x8d4c00 builds a net/http request and calls Client.do. sendScreen at 0x8d2410 similarly obtains a screen image and sends a serialized response.

runKeylogger at 0x8d1e30 opens a recording file and installs keyboard/window hooks. keyPressCallback at 0x8d17e0 writes translated keys through bufio.Writer.WriteString. windowChangeCallback at 0x8d15f0 also calls getClipboardText and writes records.

doTask at 0x8e2950 dispatches download, command execution, screen and self-removal tasks; SOCKS Serve/forward routines relay streams. staticinstall at 0x8da600 copies the image, registers scheduled task or Run-key activation, and starts the installed path.

getSystemToken at 0x8f93c0 enables privilege, locates LSASS, opens its token and calls DuplicateTokenEx. impersonateSystem at 0x8f9720 uses the token for impersonation. This supports token theft/impersonation; no LSASS memory dump is asserted.
selfDelete at 0x8fbb90 opens its own module image and calls SetFileInformationByHandle with rename information class 3 and delete-disposition class 4.

init at 0x8b7770 Base64-decodes exactly 0xad0 bytes at VA 0xa0dc90 to a 2,076-byte PowerShell script. main.main reads the decoded global string at 0xfc2490/0xfc2494, constructs a goroutine at 0x8d91a7, and gowrap3 at 0x8d9b50 passes powershell.exe and that script to shellCommand.

The decoded script excludes Program Files and AppData trees from Defender, executes reagentc /disable, downloads archive/media support tools into TEMP, and sets EnableLUA to zero via Set-ItemProperty. It is not merely an unused encoded string. The added rules cover the previously missing recovery and UAC objectives.
samples.remaining_disagreement: No material disagreement: malicious behavior and hostile classifier findings agree.
samples.material_detection_losses: None; all original hostile/suspicious findings retained.

samples.identification: Oracle Java PE carrier with appended XWorm V5.6 client
samples.reason: The appended configured RAT decrypts remote commands, invokes plugins, executes supplied/downloaded payloads, returns screenshots and implements DDoS. The Java identity of the carrier does not explain these capabilities.
samples.missing_context: Delivery, operator identity and runtime success are unknown. Static executable paths suffice for hostile intent; the Java carrier handoff remains unresolved.
samples.marker_line: XWorm V5.6: remote tasking and DDoS; add payload launch coverage
evidence: Outer file retains tnameserv.exe / Java SE 8.0.2410.7 version metadata and an Oracle certificate whose digest does not match the bytes. Its normal entry path is native Java launcher code calling JLI_Launch. The inspected carrier does not establish how execution reaches the appended client; no such runtime handoff is claimed.

Carved a 90,112-byte managed PE from file offset 0x3abd8, corresponding to the atomscan embedded:pe:XClient.exe member. dnfile/dncil method decoding, including branch targets and member references, recovered executable IL beyond strings.

Configuration decryptor at RVA 0x4ce0 derives a 32-byte AES key by copying MD5(secret) at offsets 0 and 15 (leaving final byte zero), selects ECB, Base64-decodes and decrypts config fields. Recovered config contains XWorm V5.6, its protocol delimiters, a Pastebin raw endpoint, USB.exe, %LocalAppData% and winlogon. No configured endpoint was contacted.

Startup method RVA 0x2704 copies its own bytes, writes HKCU CurrentVersion/Run, creates a Startup .lnk using WScript.Shell, sets TargetPath/WorkingDirectory and calls Save. Config controls these branches; runtime success is not claimed.

Socket Connect/BeginReceive feeds a Rijndael-decrypting dispatcher at RVA 0x3738. It handles RunShell through VisualBasic.Shell, shutdown/restart/logoff, plugin acquisition and execution. Plugin dispatcher RVA 0x3fc4 loads supplied managed bytes and invokes Run, RunRecovery, RunOptions, injRun and other entry points.

The LN branch downloads to a TEMP path (CIL local 1), then hands that same local to Process.Start. New detection matches the repeated destination local and backdoor context. Replacing the Start argument with another local removes this new trait while preserving the remaining RAT coverage.

RVA 0x48f8 loads supplied bytes into the current AppDomain, gets the entry point, prepares arguments and invokes it. This executable payload path supports the existing plugin activation finding; a concrete later plugin body is not assumed.
$Cap task captures the primary screen with CopyFromScreen, resizes to 256 by 156, encodes JPEG, compresses/Base64 encodes the buffer, and dispatches #CAP through its encrypted send method.

StartDDos/StopDDos control a threaded worker. Closure RVA 0x4974 connects a socket, sends a POST header declaring a 5,235-byte body, sleeps and disposes the connection without supplying the body. This establishes the implemented HTTP flooding behavior.
Uninstall method RVA 0x4a3c removes Run/Startup artifacts and creates a batch file that delays, deletes its own executable, then deletes the batch.

AsyncRAT third-party matches are shared User-Agent/request strings and CIL methods. Existing config.yaml exclusions already prefer independently established XWorm identity, but the native embedded-client rule only admitted .rdata. Extending it to the overlay activates the existing correction without disabling the underlying signatures.
samples.remaining_disagreement: No material disagreement: malicious behavior and hostile classifier findings agree.
samples.material_detection_losses: Two incorrect suspicious AsyncRAT attributions and unsupported XWorm-v3/Kingrat labels suppressed via existing XWorm exclusions. All concrete RAT behavior detections retained.

samples.identification: Minimal AIX Node ptrace patching demonstration
samples.reason: A minimal CLI example requests ptrace attach and a single instruction-memory write, stopping/resuming the selected PID. No executable payload, control channel, concealment, persistence or secret acquisition is present. Dangerous patching mechanics alone do not establish hostile intent.
samples.missing_context: The aix-ptrace wrapper implementation, author and deployment purpose are unavailable; no runtime success assumed.
samples.marker_line: AIX ptrace demo: process patching without payload or concealment
evidence: Read all 319 source bytes; three require imports, a PID from argv[2], openSync(`/proc/${pid}/as`, "r+"), STOP, ptrace(pid, PT_ATTACH, 0, 0), ptrace(pid, PT_WRITE_I, 0, 1), CONT, in that order.
The open result is unused. No fs.write call writes through the address-space descriptor. The old path matcher only recognizes /proc/${...}/as, independent of open mode or access.

The ptrace wrapper is not provided, so argument adaptation and runtime success are unknown. Under usual request semantics the intended write is a single value to address zero; there is no executable buffer, selected code target or redirection of the program counter.

IBM documents PT_ATTACH and PT_WRITE_I as debugging primitives. STOP and CONT change process state without terminating it. No evidence supports the old hostile evasion/injection inference. The filename suggests a positive fixture, but the verdict rests on the code rather than that filename.

Retained path and STOP/CONT command-template evidence at notable in their specific capability homes. Retained the combined memory-write profile as suspicious under process/attach/debugger. The __INJECT_CMD= text atom moved to source assignment metadata without claiming command injection.

Moved the generic Node kill-with-signal detection from termination to process/control/signal with its original matcher. Added a termination-specific structured call-argument matcher and updated its wallet-interference consumer. Explicit STOP/CONT near misses no longer imply termination; KILL/TERM positives remain.
samples.remaining_disagreement: BENIGN judgement retains a suspicious cross-process patching profile; ML probability decreased but remains high, outside the calibrated alert level grid (lvl -1). No hostile claim is restored to change classifier score.
samples.material_detection_losses: Unsupported hostile injection/evasion claim removed, with its memory-write mechanics retained as suspicious. Unsupported write-access and suspiciousness claims on a bare path and normal STOP/CONT commands corrected. No genuine attack coverage intentionally removed.
